name: Atomic JSON file repository
description: Stores one JSON file per card in a directory, writing through a temporary file and an atomic replace, and exposes a cheap change stamp from the newest modification time and file count so other processes' writes invalidate caches. Measured by the shared conformance scenarios against a temporary folder with a restart harness.
advantages: Simplest backend, no dependencies, easy to inspect and back up, crash-safe writes; fast and fully offline to measure, and the reference behaviour the other backends are compared with.
disadvantages: Single host only, no native search, and listing reads every file, which is slow at large volume; the conformance run cannot show behaviour of remote backends such as network failure or server-side paging.

name: Vector database repository
description: Stores each card as one point in a Qdrant collection, embedding it once at write time with a consumer-supplied embedder, with an optional scope payload filter so tenants cannot see each other's cards. It pages through the collection for listing and offers native card search. Measured by the same conformance scenarios on an embedded local folder with a deterministic hash embedder, closing the client on restart.
advantages: Combines persistence and semantic search without a separate index, supports tenant isolation, and runs embedded or against a server; the measurement exercises paging, restart and scope behaviour without any model or server.
disadvantages: Needs the optional dependency and an embedder, and writes cost an embedding. The server variant is not exercised by the evaluation, and a hash embedder says nothing about retrieval quality.

name: Hosted card API repository
description: Reads and writes cards through the host application's card API with a bearer key, choosing a private, team or organisation scope per call, resolving id collisions in favour of the write scope, and server-side embedding and search. Failures are logged loudly, counted and kept. Measured by the same conformance scenarios against an in-process fake of the documented card contract.
advantages: Shared across lanes and devices with server-enforced access, and no local embedding or index is needed; the measurement checks the client against the documented contract, including volume, paging and concurrent writers, without a live service. Selected because: QAR_CARDS_SCOPE and card store mounts
disadvantages: Depends on network and a running service, so latency and outages matter, and the evaluation uses a fake of the contract rather than the live service, so real server behaviour can still differ.

name: Content-hash fingerprint check
description: Pins a content hash plus modification time to each file when its card is written and recomputes the hash on query to see whether the file changed, using a modification-time fast path. No runtime arm is declared in this repository for it: the arm is the measured design (compare a stored hash of each source), so the evaluation arm stays selected.
advantages: Exact for real content changes and catches deletes, and is the production check. Selected because: FileContextStore staleness check (_current_sha)
disadvantages: Trusts an edit that restores time and size, and hashing costs a read when it runs.

name: Timestamp-and-size baseline
description: Compares modification time and size per file before and after, with no hashing.
advantages: Nearly free and trivial, so it is a good floor.
disadvantages: Misses same-size edits with restored time, and falsely flags files that were only touched.

name: Card repository with a cache seam and a null cache
description: The repository that talks to the card backend defines the cache protocol and the null cache, refreshes the listing in full or by delta, stores it after each success, offers failed writes to the cache, and serves the cached listing on a cold start during an outage while reporting degraded health.
advantages: Outages are visible but survivable, and correctness never depends on the cache.
disadvantages: The cache contract is narrow, so replay policy and conflict handling sit inside the repository, which makes it large and harder to reason about.

name: Durable file cache
description: Keeps a listing file and an outbox file in one directory, each written atomically through a temp file, with a lock for threads and swallowed I/O errors.
advantages: Survives restarts and crashes, so a cold start during an outage still serves cards and no queued write is lost. Selected because: core/selection_table.py cache-cards (default file)
disadvantages: Single-host only, so several hosts against one backend share nothing, and the file can go stale without notice.

name: No-op cache (shipped default of the seam)
description: Stores nothing and queues nothing, so every backend failure stays loud and nothing survives an outage. Used as the baseline against the live repository.
advantages: Zero state and zero risk of serving stale data, and the simplest behaviour to reason about.
disadvantages: Loses the listing and every failed write during an outage and cannot serve a cold start. Loses the listing and the outbox.

name: In-process memory cache
description: Keeps the last listing and a list of failed writes in process memory behind the same seam. It is an alternative that shows what a real cache buys.
advantages: Keeps cards and writes through a warm outage with no disk and trivial code.
disadvantages: Everything is lost on restart, so the cold-start case fails, and it is not shared across processes. Loses the listing and the outbox.

name: Durable file cache under outage scenarios
description: Plugs the file-backed cache into the same live repository in a temporary directory and runs the outage scenarios against an in-process card API, including a cold start while the backend is down.
advantages: The only arm that survives a process restart, so it is the one that passes the cold-start and lost-write cases.
disadvantages: Measures a single-host cache only, and a temporary directory hides real disk-full or permission problems. Single-host, so a card backend shared by several hosts has no shared cache.

name: Card quarantine tool
description: scripts/quarantine_cards.py reads a store and moves cards out of its index into the quarantine folder by reason: compounded copies (two or more import namespaces in the id) when a surviving card with the same files stays, cards mostly under folders the folder review excludes, surplus cards pinning the same files as a kept card, and thin cards over one generated data file. The arm runs the script with --apply over each fixture store; tests/test_quarantine_cards.py pins what it must not do.
advantages: Repairs a store that already inflated with no lane restart and no re-embedding; reversible; keeps taught and managed cards; a dry run and a manifest show every move first.
disadvantages: Runs after the fact and by an operator with access to the store's machine; does not stop the next pass from re-importing; reads a local folder store only, not the Quest backend or Qdrant.

name: Copy mode with no guard
description: The floor for prevention: nothing holds the store, so every namespaced copy a bootstrap pass adds stays in the index. Measured by the card_growth no_cleanup arm, which leaves an inflated store as copy mode left it.
advantages: Costs nothing and refuses nothing: the floor a growth guard must beat.
disadvantages: Grows with every re-import pass; duplicates crowd the view, and every copy is fingerprinted and embedded again.

name: Bootstrap guards against re-import
description: Committed on 2026-10-22 in the library itself (commit 3a59e57, with the review fixes of commits a1fff6f, 2b8e379 and ac61f64): a copy's id is made of its origin, so it cannot grow by hop and a store never imports its own cards; a store is never its own import source; every repository write refuses an id that repeats a namespace segment or is a vector point id; indexing under a root other than the store's recorded one is refused; a copy pinning the same files as a card the store holds is not kept; and the card limit (adapters/card_limit.py, QAR_MAX_CARDS, 1000 by default, 0 removes it) refuses new derived cards at the limit and announces it. The limit never trims by itself. On a local folder a new learned or quest card at the limit moves the coldest derived card into _quarantine/limit; on the Quest backend and Qdrant a learned card is admitted over the limit, because it cannot be rebuilt from the files and making room would delete shared data, while a new bootstrap card is refused, and the notice says both. The notice leads with the tidy command (repair-a-card-store) and names raising QAR_MAX_CARDS second. The card_store_growth arm builds stores through repeated passes with these guards; the card_growth arm opens an inflated store as the runner opens it, so its score on that component also includes the runner's tidy at open (repair-a-card-store:local_folder_tidy), with the self_heal setting read from config_assembler.py.
advantages: Stops compounding at its cause, on every backend, with no operator step; a refused write is logged as an error naming the id; the limit never deletes and always says what fills the store and how to change it; on a backend it never removes shared data to make room.
disadvantages: A store above its limit stays there until it is repaired (repair-a-card-store): the limit refuses, it does not trim, and on a backend learned cards keep arriving over it. Growth paths found by two reviews on 2026-10-22 and still open in committed code: copy mode is still the default (QAR_CARD_MOUNT, card_store_mounts.mount_mode_from_env); two stores keep their own folder reviews, which can disagree on the same folder with nothing reconciling them; and moving a card out leaves its vector point behind, which only context migrate-imports --prune-points removes. Closed since the reviews: what may never be moved is one definition (card_origin.protection, commit a1fff6f); a copy someone added to joins its replacement before it is retired (commit 2b8e379); one risk gate (context_risk_gate.folder_gate, commit ac61f64) is asked by every card source; and its copy-of-self signal now also flags a snapshot folder with no card store of its own (commit d00777b).

name: Risk-gated folder review
description: Committed in the library (adapters/context_risk_gate.py, commit ac61f64; the arm calls folder_gate unchanged). One cheap walk gathers structural signals with no model: three or more card stores under one folder, a series of three or more sibling folders named like dates, timestamps or versions that share one child structure, and a very large folder. A folder with a signal is always put to the folder review, below the file-count floor too, with the signal in the prompt; the verdict is cached in folder_review.json with source risk_signal and stays human-editable. When the review cannot run, a folder with a stores or series signal is not indexed, not entered, and no store beneath it is imported or mounted, with one warning naming the override. Ancestor stores in a series of copies are ignored the same way. Every card source asks this one function, and everything without a signal keeps the review as it was. A copy of the corpus itself is flagged by its copy-of-self signal (the same store id, the same recorded root, or a folder that repeats most of the root's top-level folders); since commit d00777b that layout test is asked of every folder the walk meets, so a snapshot folder with no card store of its own is flagged too, put to the review whatever the corpus size, and turned away when the review cannot run. The gate runs during bootstrap and backfill with nobody watching, so its fail-closed verdicts are the only check before a card source reads.
advantages: Keeps a snapshot series out whether or not a model is available, at the cost of one batched review call for the flagged folders; one answer for every card source; the legitimate nested store and ordinary folders are untouched; a person overrides it in the same file as every other verdict.
disadvantages: Open weaknesses: two stores keep their own folder_review.json, which can disagree on the same folder with nothing reconciling them; the large-folder signal never blocks by itself, so a huge folder with no copies is read in full when the review cannot run; a reviewer or person answering index is obeyed, so a wrong model verdict lets the series in; and it has not been run over a real backups folder of 155 stores, only over the fixture. A copy that repeats too few of the root's top-level folders, alone and with no date or version in its name, still carries no signal and is read when the review cannot run.

name: Model-judged folder review before the gate
description: The folder review as it was before the risk gate (review_corpus with no risk signals, still reachable as _folder_review): below a floor of 2,000 indexable files nothing is judged; above it the nested-repository and duplicate-tree safeguards run without a model, then batched model calls judge folders shallow first and open up only large kept or mixed ones, with verdicts cached in folder_review.json. If the review is off, has no provider or fails, nothing is excluded.
advantages: Cheap: a few batched calls per corpus, per folder not per file; keeps an unreviewable ordinary corpus fully indexed; a correct model above the floor keeps the snapshots out.
disadvantages: Fails open exactly where the risk is: with no model, the review switched off or a failed call, every snapshot store is imported or mounted and every snapshot is walked; below the floor the snapshots are never even asked about; and it decides only for the file walk's ordinary folders, so nothing names a series of copies as the reason.

name: Index everything (broken baseline)
description: No folder decision: extension filtering and the skip list only, so every folder is walked and every card store found is imported or mounted.
advantages: No model call and no rule to get wrong; nothing real is ever left out.
disadvantages: Every snapshot of a backups folder becomes cards, imports or mounts, which is the incident itself; kept only as the floor the cases must fail.

name: Repository tidy
description: adapters/card_store_tidy.py with the pure planner adapters/card_store_tidy_plan.py (the rules of scripts/quarantine_cards.py, moved into the library; the script imports them): one tidy for a local folder, the Quest backend and Qdrant, through the CardRepository port. It plans over the cards the store owns with the default reasons (vector point ids, compounded copies with a survivor, cards mostly under folders the folder review excludes, surplus cards of the same files and the same name, thin cards). Applying, it first writes a complete local export of every card it will touch and of each keeper (tidy-state under the lane's card folder, mode 600), then per keeper re-reads revisions, joins what the removed cards hold and their keywords onto the keeper, writes the keeper, and removes each card in paced batches, stopping on the first failure, then lists the store again to verify. A removed card is moved into _quarantine on a local folder and deleted on the Quest backend and Qdrant; cards tidy --undo with the run's manifest re-creates it from the export through the same port. The runner runs it at startup, in the background, when a store is over its card limit or (off a local folder) holds copies its ids prove, and RunnerConfig.card_tidy decides what happens: unset, a local folder applies and a lane with only Quest credentials (the backend) plans. With plan nothing changes: the plan is written to tidy-state/last-plan.json, with cards_after and, for a store that would still be over its limit, a second_step (the merge-topics join) with its own entries and cards_after, and it is announced once per distinct plan on the log, the startup callback and the next task's progress feed, with the apply command, the card_tidy = apply opt-in and the export and undo. With apply, the normal tidy and the merge-topics join run as one run with one export and one manifest, and what was done is announced the same way. The arm runs it on a backend-shaped store in memory (evaluation/components/card_growth/backend_fake.py), as a lane that set card_tidy = apply.
advantages: Repairs an inflated store on any backend with no operator step and no access to the machine that holds it; a lane with only Quest credentials is told the plan, the command and the opt-in on its own task feed, and nothing shared changes until its owner opts in; reversible on a backend with no quarantine folder (the export and manifest); skips a card another writer changed since the plan; a second run finds nothing; never removes a card a person wrote, used or managed, apart from provable copies whose holdings join their keeper; both steps share one export, one manifest and one undo.
disadvantages: On the Quest backend and Qdrant a removed card is deleted, not moved: shared team data, removed unattended at startup once a lane sets card_tidy = apply, and recoverable only through the export and manifest. The export sits under the lane's own card folder, on the same disk as the lane, so losing that disk loses the only copy of every deleted card. On a shared backend it only plans until the owner opts in, so a store there stays inflated until someone applies the plan. The lane does not know its own config file, so the apply command it announces for a backend store shows a placeholder for it unless QAR_CONFIG_FILE is set. The merge-topics step blurs keyword precision on the survivors, since each keeper takes the union of the keywords of the cards joined onto it (on one real store a survivor went from 7 to 123 keywords). The Quest repository path is tested with an in-memory fake (backend_fake.py and tests/test_card_store_tidy.py), not against the real Quest API. A card stored under a vector point id cannot be re-created through any repository by an undo (every writer refuses that id), so it stays in the export only. A backend undo re-writes a card through the backend, which sets its own server fields again. On a local folder the provable copies are still tidied by the tidy at open (local_folder_tidy), a second code path for the same reasons.

name: Tidy at open of a local folder
description: adapters/card_store_hygiene.py, run by FileContextStore.tidy (adapters/context_store_heal.py) when a local folder store built with self_heal opens and at the end of a pass: it moves into _quarantine/<reason> the cards that are provably copies of another card of the store (compounded ids whose files another card pins, cards pinning exactly the same files under the same name, cards stored under a vector point id, whose notes are folded into the card they were meant for), says so once, and writes a manifest beside the moved files. The runner's builders pass self_heal on since commit 1503d38. It has no arm of its own: the card_growth bootstrap_guards arm opens the inflated fixture stores with the runner's self_heal setting, so that arm's score on card_growth is this tidy's.
advantages: Needs no setting and no operator; a move, never a delete, undone by moving the file back; a clean store pays one listing of names at startup; never touches a card that was used, learned from a run or managed elsewhere.
disadvantages: A local folder only; provable copies only, so cards about excluded folders, surplus and thin cards wait for the repository tidy or the quarantine script; a second code path beside the repository tidy for the same reasons; no arm of its own, so its score is read through the bootstrap_guards arm.

name: Store as copy mode leaves it
description: Nothing is run over the store, so every namespaced copy a pass added stays in the index.
advantages: Costs nothing and touches nothing: the floor a repair must beat.
disadvantages: The store stays inflated; duplicates crowd the view, and every copy is fingerprinted and embedded again.

name: Path and title rules, no model call (floor, proposed)
description: Proposed. Metadata comes from the card's own title and sources; files are placed by path prefix.
advantages: No cost, deterministic.
disadvantages: Misses meaning that is not in the path; not built.

name: QAR card repository
description: Keeps hub cards in a QAR card repository, mapping a card's text to the summary, its tags to keywords and its source to provenance, and delegating add, get, search, delete and count to the repository.
advantages: Any repository, files or the Quest API, can stand in the hub's card-store seat, so a hub consumer gets QAR's persistence without a second store.
disadvantages: The consumer must pass the repository in; search reads every stored card and matches the query words as substrings, with no ranked selection.

name: Quest backend card API from the environment
description: Keeps hub cards in the Quest backend card API named by QUEST_BASE_URL and QUEST_API_KEY, so a consumer with a Quest account passes no repository.
advantages: Nothing to pass once the Quest keys are set; the cards live where every Quest deployment keeps them.
disadvantages: Needs a reachable Quest backend; a consumer that keeps cards elsewhere passes qar-card-repository with its own repository.

name: Per-lane assembly of the context members (today)
description: The lane's context assembler, reference resolver, mixed card and specification search and vector index, each handed in as a seat and built on first use; each line delegates to the member that owns it.
advantages: Built; adds nothing before the reply and changes nothing the lane's assembler returns; the members stay separately measured and swappable.
disadvantages: The assembler the lane runs is still chosen in the lane's configuration, not by this arm.
